req.title: Health probe returns liveness
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and a status:'ok' JSON body.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /health/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing status:'ok'. To achieve high mutation kill rate we need: (1) a positive EP test asserting exact status code 200 AND exact JSON body {'status':'ok'}; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that an unsupported method (POST) on /health/ returns 405, not 200, catching any mutation that makes the route accept all methods; (3) a BVA boundary test asserting the Content-Type header is application/json, catching mutations that change the response format; (4) a DT test asserting the response body key is exactly 'status' and value is exactly 'ok' (not 'OK', not 'okay'), catching string-constant mutations; (5) a STC test verifying the endpoint is idempotent across two consecutive calls, catching any stateful mutation that changes behaviour after first invocation.

tests.name: test_health_returns_200_and_status_ok_body
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
health_route is registered on the app
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_returns_200_and_status_ok_body():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body == {"status": "ok"}
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert len(body) == 1

test_health_returns_200_and_status_ok_body()

trace: R-PLAYER-016: status:'ok' — exact string constant must match
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_status_value_exact_string_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert "status" in body
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert body["status"] != "OK"
    assert body["status"] != "okay"
    assert body["status"] != True
    assert body["status"] != 1

test_health_status_value_exact_string_ok()

health_route is registered on the app
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
expected: Both calls return identical JSON body {"status": "ok"}
trace: R-PLAYER-016: endpoint must be stateless and idempotent
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_idempotent_across_two_calls():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.get("/health/")
    r2 = client.get("/health/")
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r1.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r2.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r1.json() == r2.json()

test_health_idempotent_across_two_calls()
